title: Simultaneous finite evaluation witnesses without a pairing equation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a field $k$ in which $\ell$ is invertible, and a separated finite-type morphism $a:X\to Y$ of finite-type $k$-schemes. Fix a compactification $c$ of $a$, a normalized system projection-evaluation model $m$ and a scalar specialization $s$ [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation]. For every $n\in\mathbf N$, there exists finite comparison data $e:\operatorname{FiniteEvaluation}(\ell,E,m,s,n)$ [def-coef-finite-pairing-evaluation-data]. Thus the ordinary pure-section, signed tensor-localization, sections-unit, adjunction-unit/counit, pullback-composition, open chain-map and cartesian-Hom comparison equations all hold simultaneously. This statement does not assert any equation for the composite pairing $m.\beta$. The finite coefficient exponent is $n+1$ [def-coef-finite-projection-evaluation-data].

proof.text: For each of X,Y,Z and the point, use the actual ordinary quotient evaluation and pure-tensor comparison. Its signed total-complex comparison descends by universal tensor localization. Compare it with the fixed system and finite tensor models by their prescribed representative normalizations; this gives x,y,z,quotient,integral and their pure-section equations and symmetry squares.

proof.text: Evaluate the actual ordinary sections, proper pushforward and scalar restriction squares. Their universal derived-unit normalizations give sectionsX and sectionsY and the right-adjoint comparisons. Transport the adjunctions along these squares: the evaluated ordinary units and counits descend to gxUnit, gxCounit, gyUnit, gyCounit, rUnit, rCounit, properUnit and properCounit. The tensor comparison on pure sections gives the four strong tensor equations. This uses separate right-derived comparisons, not preservation of K-injectives by varying-ring evaluation.

proof.text: The reduction model of s identifies s.reduced K with scalar extension of the constant K tower. Associativity makes it cartesian. The system cartesian-first-input Hom evaluation formula gives the finite Hom isomorphism for arbitrary N; its tensor-Hom transpose is coefficientBaseChangeHom, giving hom_normalization. Assemble all these normalized witnesses in FiniteEvaluation.

theorem finiteEvaluation_exists
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u})
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (a : X ⟶ Y) [a.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated a] [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a]
    (_hl : IsUnit (l : k)) (c : Compactification a)
    (m : Model l E c) (s : ScalarSpecialization l E m) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (FiniteEvaluation l E m s n)
